comment: How the player is built, once, for every target. scripts/build_player.py builds it; scripts/prepare_rmlui.py builds the same RmlUi (and FreeType) for the tests. A difference between platforms or targets is a key under one here, never a second script. A target's processor is the part of its name after the platform, as Apple's tools spell it (-arch, lipo).

universal.comment: A player made of several targets' builds, one slice each, joined into one file (lipo -create). Each slice is built as its own target, in a folder named for it inside the universal build; the macOS kit is made from the joined player. Which slices a file holds is read from the file (lipo -archs), never from this list.

deploymentTarget.comment: The oldest system a platform's player runs on. Every slice, and the RmlUi and FreeType linked into it, is compiled and linked for it: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for configure, cmake and the compilers, and the fork's MINVERFLAGS, which otherwise names a version of its own per processor. 11.0 is the arm64 floor.

freetype.comment: Built from its pinned release for every target and linked into the player statically, so no platform's kit carries a FreeType library.

sdl2.comment: SDL2, which the Mac player reads controllers through (drivers.macos.joypad): it drives each model's rumble, the DualSense's included, which RetroArch's own HID driver does not. The Windows launcher links it too (launcher.sdl2): it reads a sandboxed game's controllers through DirectInput for the game, and DirectInput cannot rumble a DualSense or an Xbox pad, so the launcher rumbles them through SDL (desktop/src-tauri/launcher/windows/pad_relay.c). Built from its pinned release for each slice and linked statically, with only its controller parts (the fork compiles no SDL video driver on the Mac); what else it links, all of it the system's, is read from the sdl2.pc it installs. configure finds it through INCLUDES and LDFLAGS (scripts/native_build.py, sdl2_environment).

configure.comment: Two OpenGL drivers, one player for every game: gl runs GLSL shaders, glcore (opengl_core) runs slang, compiled with the fork's own glslang and SPIRV-Cross (builtinglslang). glslang and SPIRV-Cross are left for configure to settle: --enable-glslang makes it look for a system glslang and stop. A game's shader language picks the driver (shader_format.rs). TLS is RetroArch's own client (retrossl, on libretro-common/crypto), built into the player on every platform; configure would otherwise take a system mbedTLS or BearSSL it finds, which on a Mac is Homebrew's and exists for one processor only. RetroArch's own video and audio codecs for its movie player and recording (WebM, MP4, VP9, MPEG-1, Opus, AAC) and its WebP and DDS images are left out, and so are its SMB and NFS network file clients, because no game uses them and they make the player larger.
configure.comment-environment: On a Mac configure uses no pkg-config (PKG_CONF_PATH=none, a switch of the fork's configure): it finds a library by linking a test program against it, which reaches only the SDK's libraries, the system's zlib among them. pkg-config would offer any library Homebrew installed, which exists for one processor only. The RmlUi part of the fork's makefile still uses pkg-config for FreeType, which returns the FreeType built beside it.
configure.comment-windows: No WinMM: it is only RetroArch's MIDI output, which the macOS player does not have (its build never enables CoreMIDI, so its MIDI driver is null), and it opens the system's synthesiser at every start, which slows the launch.

comment-checkout: How git writes the fork into a build folder. Windows makes no symbolic link without extra rights (the fork's are inside Apple bundles, which Windows never builds), and some of the fork's paths are longer than 260 characters there.

makefile.comment-common: HAVE_CONFIG_MK turns off the makefile's stop when configure's sources are newer than config.mk: the build's configure.mk runs configure again whenever they are, and configure keeps an unchanged config.mk as it was.
makefile.comment-macos: dead_strip removes the functions nothing calls, which makes the Mac player smaller.
makefile.comment-windows: Os: the player's own code is optimised for size, which makes it smaller without slowing emulation, because the core does the work. RmlUi stays Release: built MinSizeRel it requires a std::string constructor the static C++ runtime does not have. -ffunction-sections with --gc-sections makes the player larger with this toolchain.

platformFolders.comment: The folders, inside a folder of ROM-in-a-Box's own C sources, that hold a platform's own sources, beside the shared ones at its top: the folder named for the platform, and posix/, what macOS and Linux share. The launcher's sources and the QUICK SIGN IN store's are laid out this way (scripts/native_build.py, platform_sources).

accounts.comment: ROM-in-a-Box's own sources the player compiles, the QUICK SIGN IN store: those at the top of `folder`, which every platform shares, and the platform's own in the folders platformFolders names for it (sealed.c: windows/ seals a token with DPAPI, posix/ keeps it as it is). scripts/native_build.py hands them over, with the headers at the top, and the launcher's file layer they are built on (portable_fs), as the target's platform has it, and the fork compiles every C file it is handed.

capabilities.comment: A function each player must have, read from the linked player before it is stripped: the achievements client, and RetroArch's TLS socket layer, which achievements reach their service through. The player links no library outside the system, so its TLS is the one built into it.

drivers.comment: What an exported game's player is told to use, per platform: its audio driver, its controller driver, and the controller profile folders RetroArch reads. A pad's profiles are read from the folder named for the driver it was connected under; on Windows that driver connects XInput pads as xinput and every other pad as dinput. The exporter writes audio and joypad into the game's settings; scripts/build_kit.py stages joypadProfiles from the pinned autoconfig archive (scripts/prepare_runtime.py).

systemLibraries.comment: The libraries every machine of a platform has, so a player, a launcher or a core may import them. The Windows list covers every import of the catalog's Windows cores, as published on the buildbot, and of the builder. scripts/build_player.py rejects a player, launcher or preview renderer that imports anything else, scripts/build_builder.py a builder or command line, and an export rejects such a core. On Windows a library is named by its file name, in lower case, and Windows also resolves any api-ms-win- API set; on macOS by its path, and the system's are those under these folders.

launcher.comment: The game's launcher, for a target that runs it as its own program: its shared sources at the top of desktop/src-tauri/launcher, and those in the folders platformFolders names for the target's platform: its entry, in the folder named for the platform, and its file layer, portable_fs, and the way a launch plan's paths read, paths.c, in posix/ (what macOS and Linux share) or windows/. A macOS kit carries its launcher as a library the player loads (launchLibrary). sdl2: whether the launcher links the recipe's SDL2, built for the target beside it.

fork.comment: The fork's code the launcher links, compiled as the fork's own, without the launcher's warnings: the zstd decoder a game made into one program unpacks itself with (launcher/windows/unpack.c), without its assembly.

launchLibrary.comment: On macOS the launcher is a library the player loads before its main: it prepares the launch and hands main the arguments (launcher/macos/arguments.c), from the launcher's sources for the platform (platformFolders). It is built when the macOS kit is made (scripts/build_kit.py), for every slice of the kit's player and the platform's deployment target, and attached to each slice of the kit's player then (scripts/native_runtime/inject_dylib.c): nothing about it depends on a game. The kit carries it as its launcher; an export copies the two, thinned for a game that runs on Apple silicon alone, and signs them. 'libraries' are the system's it links, for the library and for the plan tool built from the same sources (scripts/launcher_plan.py): CoreFoundation puts up the alert that tells a person why a game cannot start.

fileLayer.comment: libretro's file layer, which the menu reads and writes its files through with UTF-8 paths on every platform, named from the fork's root. Every program built from the menu's sources links it. The config reader, file/config_file.c, is not part of it, so a test program can stand in for that boundary.

preview.comment: The builder's menu preview, rml-preview: the player's own RmlUi renderer drawing a composed menu into a picture, in an OpenGL context on a window never shown, built beside the player from the same fork, RmlUi and FreeType, and with the file layer above. 'sources' are the repository's, 'forkSources' the fork's; a target adds its entry, which reads the program's arguments as that platform passes them, and its OpenGL context. The menu GL probe (test_dcmenu.py) draws in the same context. It links FreeType statically, as the player does, so it is copied into the builder's resources alone. It is built for the builder's own processor only, never joined into a universal file.

kit.comment: What scripts/build_kit.py puts in a target's runtime kit besides the assets every kit carries (scripts/kit_assets.py). A file is named by its role, which the exporter reads it by, and says where in the kit it goes; build: is a file in the player build (in a universal build, the folder holding the joined player). made:launcher is the launch library scripts/build_kit.py builds for a kit whose target the recipe declares one for (launchLibrary), and attaches to the kit's player. The licences of what the player is made from come from licenses/ (scripts/licences.py): those of every library the build compiled, and of the target's platform's runtime. 'libraryInventory' names the folder and the inventory the macOS exporter reads a kit's libraries from (packaging/macos.rs): the player links none, so the folder is empty and the inventory lists no file.
